summary: FMC's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-27) presents a coordinated distress profile: (a) two covenant amendments in 5 months (Jun + Nov 2023) loosening max leverage from 3.5x to 6.50x with share-repurchase suspension through Sep 2025, (b) three putative securities class actions filed within 28 days (Nov-Dec 2023) alleging non-disclosure of patent-protection diminishment in India/China/Brazil — the very markets where the FY2023 10-K now admits 'we have not obtained that requested relief, allowing products to be launched,' (c) Project Focus global restructuring announced Dec 15 2023, (d) 23% revenue decline accelerating to 32% in Q1'24 with NA -48% in Q1'24, (e) leverage moving the wrong way (4.17x year-end -> 5.71x Q1'24) relative to the covenant step-down to 3.75x by Sep 2025. Mode B inferences dominate: the diamide franchise (39% of revenue) is structurally exposed to composition-of-matter expirations that BEGIN in early 2024 (the guidance year), and the 2024 EBITDA guidance requires a 26-point YoY inflection between Q1 and the rest of the year that has no quantified buildup. Counter-signals are clean KPMG audit (96-year tenure, no material weakness, no going-concern) and zero insider open-market sales in 2024 YTD. Net read: SHORT-tier — claim-evolution velocity is high, multiple SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY signals reinforce a single causal mechanism (patent erosion -> diamide volume/price decline -> EBITDA collapse -> covenant relief -> share-repurchase suspension -> securities litigation), and the rebuttal evidence is concentrated in audit quality and insider quietness, both of which are weaker as forward indicators than the credit-and-litigation pattern.
